title: Boston Cream Pie
summary: Two layers of light vanilla sponge filled with silky pastry cream and finished with a poured chocolate glaze that drips down the sides.
equipment: two 20 cm round cake tins, greased and base-lined
stand mixer or electric hand whisk

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt
cake flour (or plain flour; see note)
ingredients.note: plain flour works with a slightly firmer crumb

ingredients.item: dark chocolate (about 60% cocoa solids), finely chopped

steps.title: Make the pastry cream
steps.text: Heat the milk in a saucepan until steaming, then whisk the egg yolks, sugar, cornflour and salt together in a bowl until pale. Pour the hot milk into the yolk mixture in a thin stream, whisking constantly, so the eggs warm gradually rather than scrambling.

steps.title: Cook the custard
steps.text: Return the mixture to the pan and cook over medium heat, whisking constantly, until it thickens and starts to bubble; keep it bubbling for 1 minute more. That full minute of boiling cooks out the raw starch so the custard sets firm, and brings it safely above 74°C.

steps.title: Chill the custard
steps.text: Off the heat, whisk in the butter and vanilla, then push the custard through a sieve into a bowl to catch any lumps. Press cling film directly onto the surface and chill for at least 3 hours, until completely cold and firm. Chilling flat against the surface stops a skin forming while it sets.

steps.title: Preheat the oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 175°C (155°C fan) with a shelf in the middle, allowing at least 20 minutes for it to reach temperature before the sponge goes in.

steps.title: Whisk the egg mixture
steps.text: Whisk the eggs, sugar and salt on high speed for 4-5 minutes, until thick, pale and roughly doubled in volume, then mix in the vanilla. This whipped-egg method is what gives the sponge its light, airy texture without extra butter.

steps.title: Fold in the flour
steps.text: Sift the flour and baking powder over the whisked eggs and fold in gently in two additions. Folding rather than stirring vigorously keeps the air you've just whipped in from collapsing.

steps.title: Temper in the warm milk
steps.text: Heat the milk and butter together until hot but not boiling, then stir a spoonful of the batter into it to loosen it. Fold this mixture back into the rest of the batter until just combined, which keeps the sponge from deflating.

steps.title: Bake the sponges
steps.text: Divide the batter between the two tins and bake for 20-25 minutes, until golden and springy to the touch. Cool in the tins for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a rack and leave to cool completely before filling.

steps.title: Fill the cake
steps.text: Whisk the cold pastry cream briefly to loosen it back to a smooth, spreadable texture. Set one sponge layer on a serving plate, spread the pastry cream to within 1cm of the edge, then top with the second layer and press down gently.

steps.title: Make the glaze
steps.text: Bring the double cream and golden syrup just to the boil, then pour over the chopped chocolate and leave undisturbed for 2 minutes. Stir until completely smooth and glossy; the resting time lets the chocolate melt gently rather than seizing from direct heat.

steps.title: Glaze and chill
steps.text: Let the glaze cool for 5-10 minutes until it thickens slightly, then pour it onto the centre of the cake and nudge it gently so it reaches the edge and drips down the sides. Chill for 30 minutes to set the glaze before slicing, and keep the cake refrigerated afterwards.

tips: Keep whisking constantly once the custard starts to bubble, and let it bubble for the full minute – stopping early leaves it starchy and thin instead of properly set.
Press cling film directly onto the surface of the warm pastry cream so a skin doesn't form while it chills.
Let the sponge layers cool completely before filling, or residual warmth will melt the pastry cream and it will slide out the sides.
Pour the glaze while it's still slightly warm and fluid, or it won't settle into an even, glossy layer.
Keep the finished cake refrigerated throughout, since it's filled with an egg custard.
safety: Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Store in the fridge, covered, for up to 3 days, as the custard filling needs to stay cold. It isn't suitable for freezing once filled, as the pastry cream can separate when thawed.
